guidelines.detail: documentation rule FID-03 not applied (The description identifies the process trigger and terminal outcome, while the generated labels are generic. Documented guideline FID-03 already advises meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events; learned guidelines LRN-005 and LRN-012 also cover these cases.)

same as LRN-017 (The description identifies refund and replacement as alternatives, while M4 records a missing gateway after those activities. This supports modeling alternative paths; learned guideline LRN-017 already states essentially the same rule.)

same as LRN-005 (The description identifies a customer order as a process trigger and failed payment as an ending outcome, while the matched reference labels are generic. This supports meaningful event labels. The guideline is already covered by learned guidance for start-event labels (LRN-005) and end-event labels (LRN-012).)

refines ACT-05 (The records indicate that the generated start event represents the report described as triggering the continuation, while the reference places the report within the ongoing process. Modeling its receipt as an intermediate message catch event preserves that flow and distinguishes a message occurrence from performed work, refining ACT-05.)

documentation rule FID-03 not applied (The generated labels generally preserve details stated in the description, while the reference uses generic event labels or less specific activity labels. FID-03 already advises short, faithful labels and meaningful event triggers or outcomes.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that several activities are all required before a later activity or outcome: Model the activities as parallel branches and synchronize all branches with a parallel gateway before the later activity or outcome.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that two or more required activities follow the same activity, without specifying an order between them

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description explicitly states the occurrence that starts the process or the outcome that marks it as complete

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents two or more distinct activities as alternatives: Model each activity as a separate task on its own branch rather than combining the alternatives into one task; choose a gateway that matches whether one or multiple alternatives may be performed.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents two or more distinct activities as mutually exclusive alternatives

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an occurrence that starts the process: Label the start event with a concise phrase naming that trigger rather than a generic label.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a specific event that starts the process or an outcome that ends it

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a report or message from an external participant conditionally triggers a continuation within an already-running process: Model receipt of the report as an intermediate message catch event in the existing process, rather than as a task or a new start event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a report or message from an external participant conditionally triggers a continuation within an already-running process
